> Are we sure selector spread didn't somehow get slower?

I'm not quite sure. The background is that in the early days of 1.17 release, Aldo showed me a perf comparison that showed the selector spread performs much better, but now it seems the result gets reversed.

I mean the optimization on lableSelector (the internal version of `topologySpreadConstraint`).

issue_context.title: Move Pod Spread priority logic to its Score plugin [Migration Phase 2]
issue_context.body:
/assign @Huang-Wei 
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon

This includes moving the metadata logic into PostFilter.

Part of #85822

review_comments:
This is the unfair part to SelectorSpreadPriority.

This calculation should be taken into account in the benchmark.
shouldn't this node have a score of zero already? why do we need to set it explicitly?
Technically this line can be removed, however, explicitly setting it to 0 doesn't hurt and make the code easy to read.
does this really need to be outside the test function?

Technically no. I just moved them as they were - from `priorities/spreading_perf_test.go`, as the intention was to use the same test cases to compare the perf of pod topology spread and default selector spreading. I believe once @alculquicondor done the migration of selector spreading, we can find a better place to hold it.
why? the score is zero anyways, right?

It's "invalid" (as explained https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/86684#discussion_r361819269), which should only be finalized to 0 at L228~L231; otherwise, it would be treated as a node which has 0 matching pods.
